subject: DPA: incident triggers, routing matrix & country export responsibilities
messages:
From: Alex Li <alex.li@novamed.com>

Cc: Sam Choi <sam.choi@novamed.com>, Novamed Security <security@novamed.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Possible exposure of a subset of telemetry from test environment

Hi Tessa —

Quick heads up: our security team flagged an S3 bucket that contained anonymized telemetry from a Redwood integration test run. We believe the data set is limited (no PHI, sample IDs only) but it includes model request/response artifacts from a non-production tenant.

Were pausing ingestion and will share a short summary shortly. Novamed's DPA has a 48-hour cooperative window for evidence requests and the security team asked whether Redwood has an agreed routing matrix (who we call for forensics, who shares exports, and subprocessors that might have copies).

Would you confirm next steps and contact points? We can provide an initial export if that helps.

Thanks,
Alex
Security Ops, Novamed

Attachments: none

From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@novamed.com>

Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 09:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible exposure of a subset of telemetry from test environment

Hi Alex — thanks for the ping and for flagging.

Short answer: we have a DPA clause that requires cooperative assistance within 48 hours for evidence preservation and a separate clause on subprocessor involvement for forensic exports. What Id like to confirm quickly: scope (production vs test), PID/PHI exposure (you said none), and whether Novamed needs a full forensic export or tokenized summaries.

Kimberly — tagging you for contract/DPA interpretation and for whether Novameds 48h cooperative ask triggers our standard export SLA or needs an exec exception. Ben/Marissa — FYI on subprocessors: if any telemetry was routed to a storage or analytics subprocessor, we need to identify them and whether they hold copies. Im attaching a draft "incident trigger matrix" (v1) that maps trigger types to who owns the outreach/export.

Proposed immediate steps (can we confirm within 2 hours?):
- Alex: confirm dataset name and bucket region + whether any customers other than Novamed were in the same test run
- Novamed Security: share a one-pager with the indicators (hashes or filenames)
- Kimberley/legal: confirm whether we should treat this as a DPA-level cooperative export or a lower-touch telemetry summary
- Ben: run a quick subprocessor hit-check (storage/analytics/backup) and flag any copies

Ill coordinate a short bridge if helpful.

—Tessa
Director, Incident Coordination | Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident_trigger_matrix_v1.xlsx (see tab: routing proposal)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Alex Li <alex.li@novamed.com>

Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible exposure of a subset of telemetry from test environment

Tessa / Alex —

Thanks. Based on Alex's note (test environment, no PHI), this initially falls under our DPA cooperative assistance obligations but does not trigger the full 72-hour formal breach notification timeline reserved for confirmed customer-impacting incidents with personal data exfiltration. Action items from a contract lens:

1) Provide Novamed a secure export of the artifacts they request within the cooperative window (48 hours). This is an assistance obligation; we should avoid over-sharing and prefer tokenized or hashed artifacts unless Novamed demonstrates need for full payloads.
2) If any subprocessor holds replicas, we must coordinate evidence collection through them but we do not automatically need to notify regulatory bodies unless we confirm personal data exfiltration.
3) Log every step in our incident tracker (JIRA PRIV-4742).

Ben: please confirm whether S3/analytics/backup subprocessors have copies. If so, we need the subprocessor contact and a timeline for export. We should also prepare an escalation path if Novamed requests a signed export acceptance or chain-of-custody stamp.

Alex: please confirm the specific artifact identifiers and whether Novamed will accept a redacted export or needs raw files. We will treat their cooperative window as high priority.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory_redline.docx (proposed fields to collect)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Li <alex.li@novamed.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 12:13:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible exposure of a subset of telemetry from test environment

Quick update from infra: we ran a subprocessor hit-check across our storage and analytics pipelines. Findings:
- Primary S3 (us-west-2) held the bucket; no cross-account replication configured.
- Backup snapshots: backup vendor (CloudKeep Inc.) retained a snapshot window that might contain the artifacts.
- Analytics pipeline: hashed telemetry was forwarded to DataSense (analytics subprocessor) for anonymized metric computation; we do not store raw request/response there.

Next steps:
- Ill open the subprocessor request with CloudKeep and request an isolated export within 6 hours; Ill include chain-of-custody details and ask for MD5 hashes.
- DataSense can produce hashed telemetry extracts; if Novamed accepts hashes, that should be quick (2-4 hours).

Marissa — can you prepare a short consent wording we can send to Novamed that offers redacted extracts first and reserves the option to provide fuller payloads under an executed evidence transfer letter? We want to avoid unnecessary legal exposure.

Ben
Senior Infrastructure Ops | Redwood Inference

Summary: 
- Scope: non-production/test bucket in us-west-2; no PHI; artifacts are model request/response logs for a test tenant tied to Novamed integration.
- Subprocessors: CloudKeep (backup) may retain snapshots; DataSense holds hashed analytics (no raw requests).
- Contractual posture: Redwood will comply with the DPA cooperative assistance clause and provide tokenized/hashes first. Full payloads require an evidence transfer letter and chain-of-custody acceptance.

Immediate deliverables (next 24 hours):
1) Ben: isolated export of hashes + associated metadata from DataSense (ETA: 3 hours).
2) Ben: CloudKeep request for a snapshot export and MD5s (ETA: 6 hours).
3) Marissa/Kimberly: suggested consent/acceptance wording for a redacted export + optional evidence transfer letter (ETA: 2 hours).
4) Tessa: I will share an updated incident trigger matrix that explicitly maps who owns cross-border export approvals and subprocessor coordination (link below).

Novamed ask: please confirm whether you will accept hashed/tokenized artifacts for your preliminary triage. If you require raw payloads, indicate why so we can route the request through the evidence transfer flow.

Link to updated matrix (draft): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-trigger-matrix
JIRA: PRIV-4742

Thanks all — Ill update the thread as we get artifacts.
